concepts.name: Definition and Rationale of Priority Sector Lending (PSL)
key_dimensions: Sectors classified as 'priority' and the economic rationale behind their inclusion
Historical evolution: from Narsimham Committee recommendations to current RBI Master Directions
Distinction between PSL as a regulatory mandate vs. commercial banking objective
Who prescribes PSL norms: RBI's authority under Banking Regulation Act vs. government advisories

concepts.name: Overall PSL Target: 40% Mandate and Bank-wise Differentiation
key_dimensions: 40% of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) or Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure (CEOBE), whichever is higher
Differential targets for Domestic Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) vs. Foreign Banks with 20+ branches vs. Foreign Banks with fewer than 20 branches
Small Finance Banks (SFBs): 75% PSL target — the highest among all bank categories
Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) and Cooperative Banks: applicability and specific sub-targets

concepts.name: Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC): Computation and Significance
key_dimensions: Formula: Net Bank Credit + investments in non-SLR bonds held in HTM category — certain deductions
Why ANBC is the base for PSL calculation rather than total advances
CEOBE as an alternative base: when it applies and how it is calculated
Common UPSC trap: confusing ANBC with Net Bank Credit or Total Credit

concepts.name: Sub-targets within PSL: Agriculture Sector
key_dimensions: 18% of ANBC for Agriculture overall; sub-target of 10% for Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs)
Distinction between direct agriculture lending (crop loans, farm infrastructure) and indirect agriculture lending (agri-input dealers, cold chains)
Allied activities included under agriculture: animal husbandry, fisheries, beekeeping
UPSC trap: only direct agriculture counts toward the 10% SMF sub-target, not indirect

concepts.name: Sub-targets for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)
key_dimensions: 7.5% of ANBC earmarked for Micro Enterprises specifically (not MSMEs broadly)
Revised MSME classification post-2020: investment and turnover criteria replacing older investment-only criteria
Distinction: Medium enterprises qualify for PSL but have no dedicated sub-target
Overlap with 'Weaker Sections' category — some MSME loans can be double-counted

concepts.name: Sub-target for Weaker Sections
key_dimensions: 12% of ANBC dedicated to Weaker Sections including SC/ST, women (loans up to ₹1 lakh), minorities, SHGs, etc.
Specific beneficiary categories notified by RBI and their qualifying loan limits
Overlap with agriculture and MSME sub-targets: same loan can satisfy multiple sub-targets
UPSC trap: 'Weaker Sections' is a PSL sub-target, not a standalone sector

concepts.name: Housing Sector under PSL: Loan Limits and Conditions
key_dimensions: Loans up to ₹35 lakh in metropolitan centres and ₹25 lakh in other centres qualify (subject to overall cost caps)
Repair of housing units: separate and lower loan limits (₹10 lakh metropolitan, ₹6 lakh others)
Loans to housing finance companies (HFCs) for on-lending: indirect PSL treatment
Distinction: PSL housing loans vs. Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) — not the same

concepts.name: Education Loans under PSL
key_dimensions: Loans up to ₹20 lakh for studies in India and abroad qualify under PSL
Only loans to individuals qualify — loans to institutions do not
Distinction from Vidya Lakshmi Portal and Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme
UPSC trap: no sub-target for education within PSL; it falls under the overall 40%

concepts.name: Renewable Energy Sector under PSL
key_dimensions: Loans up to ₹30 crore for solar, biomass, wind energy projects qualify
Individual household loans for renewable energy (e.g., solar panels) up to ₹10 lakh
Addition of renewable energy as a PSL category reflecting green finance push post-2015
Distinction: renewable energy PSL vs. RBI's green deposit/taxonomy framework

concepts.name: Social Infrastructure under PSL
key_dimensions: Covers schools, health care facilities, drinking water, sanitation in Tier II–VI centres
Loan limit: up to ₹5 crore per borrower
Rationale: bridging public investment gaps in rural and semi-urban social infrastructure
UPSC trap: loans for social infrastructure in Tier I cities (metros) do NOT qualify

concepts.name: Export Credit under PSL (Foreign Banks)
key_dimensions: Foreign banks with fewer than 20 branches: export credit up to 32% of ANBC counts toward PSL
Domestic banks: export credit does NOT count toward PSL (common UPSC trap)
Rationale for differential treatment of foreign banks with limited branch presence
Interaction with RBI's Export Credit Refinance (ECR) facility (now discontinued)

concepts.name: Priority Sector Lending Certificates (PSLCs): Mechanism and Types
key_dimensions: Four types: PSLC-Agriculture, PSLC-Small and Marginal Farmers, PSLC-Micro Enterprises, PSLC-General
Buyer-seller mechanism: banks exceeding targets sell PSLCs to banks falling short — no transfer of underlying loan risk
Trading platform: RBI's e-Kuber platform used for PSLC transactions
UPSC trap: PSLCs transfer the 'achievement' of PSL target, NOT the loan asset itself

concepts.name: Non-Achievement of PSL Targets: Consequences and RIDF
key_dimensions: Shortfall contribution to Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF) maintained with NABARD
Differential penalty: shortfall in overall PSL goes to RIDF/other funds; shortfall in sub-targets has separate fund allocations (MSME: SIDBI, Housing: NHB)
Interest rate on RIDF deposits is below market rate — an implicit cost/penalty for banks
UPSC trap: RIDF contributions are not a 'fine' but low-yield mandatory deposits

concepts.name: NABARD's Role in PSL: Refinance and Oversight
key_dimensions: NABARD provides refinance to RRBs, Cooperative Banks, and SCBs for agriculture and rural lending
NABARD administers RIDF and allocates funds for rural infrastructure projects
NABARD's annual inspection of RRBs and oversight of PSL compliance in cooperative sector
Distinction: NABARD regulates cooperative banks' PSL compliance; RBI regulates SCBs and SFBs

concepts.name: On-Lending Model and PSL Classification
key_dimensions: Banks lending to NBFC-MFIs, SFBs, and other eligible intermediaries for on-lending to priority sectors qualifies as PSL
Loan limits for on-lending: ₹20 lakh per borrower for agriculture, ₹20 lakh for others
UPSC trap: on-lending through NBFCs (other than NBFC-MFIs) has restricted PSL eligibility
Sunset clause concept: RBI periodically reviews and may withdraw on-lending PSL classification

concepts.name: Microfinance and NBFC-MFI Lending under PSL
key_dimensions: Loans by banks to NBFC-MFIs for on-lending to low-income households qualify as PSL under indirect agriculture/weaker sections
RBI's 2022 Microfinance Directions: income ceiling for microfinance borrowers set at ₹3 lakh household income
Distinction between MFI PSL loans and SHG-Bank Linkage Programme (SBLP) loans
UPSC trap: NBFC-MFI loans qualify as PSL for the lending bank, not for the NBFC itself (NBFCs have no PSL obligation)

concepts.name: Small Finance Banks (SFBs) and PSL: Special Obligations
key_dimensions: SFBs must maintain 75% PSL — highest mandate — with 40% to smaller sub-categories
SFBs were specifically licensed to serve unbanked/underbanked segments, hence higher PSL obligation
Sub-target: at least 40% of total PSL must go to sectors eligible under Weaker Sections and micro enterprises
UPSC trap: SFBs' PSL base is also ANBC or CEOBE, same as SCBs — not deposits

concepts.name: Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) and Cooperative Banks: PSL Framework
key_dimensions: RRBs: 75% PSL target, same as SFBs, reflecting their rural mandate
State Cooperative Banks and District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs): 40% PSL target
Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs): RBI has separate PSL guidelines with 40% target and distinct sub-targets
UPSC trap: Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are not directly subject to RBI's PSL norms

concepts.name: PSL and Financial Inclusion: Linkage with Jan Dhan, Mudra, and Stand-Up India
key_dimensions: MUDRA loans (Shishu, Kishore, Tarun) up to ₹10 lakh qualify as PSL under Micro Enterprises
Stand-Up India loans to SC/ST and women entrepreneurs (₹10 lakh–₹1 crore) qualify under Weaker Sections PSL
Jan Dhan overdrafts (up to ₹10,000): qualify as PSL under Weaker Sections
UPSC trap: MUDRA loans qualify as PSL only if the borrower is a micro enterprise; larger loans under Tarun (₹5–10 lakh) are at the boundary

concepts.name: PSL Norms for Payment Banks and Local Area Banks
key_dimensions: Payment Banks: cannot lend, hence PSL norms are NOT applicable — a critical UPSC exception
Local Area Banks (LABs): subject to PSL norms similar to RRBs given their regional rural focus
New Umbrella Entities (NUEs) proposed: PSL applicability still under deliberation
UPSC trap: conflating Payment Banks' investment obligations (75% in SLR securities) with PSL obligations
